(I) BRIEF FACTS:-
1.) This judgment shall decide the reference petition no.
7/2018 preferred by petitioner, Sh. Rajesh for the enhancement of the compensation against compulsory acquisition of their shop/building bearing No.1/1142-A comprised in khasra No.446 Min. situated at Main Market, Railway Road, Shahdara, Delhi having area around 16.7 sq. meters each vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999, passed by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as 'LAC'), Shahdara, Delhi.
2.)

To decide the reference U/s 18 L.A. Act r/w statement U/s 19 of the Act sent by the LAC Delhi,
the relevant dates and facts which are necessary for adjudication in the present matter are being given herein under:-
i) Date of notification U/s 4 of the Act : 12.06.1997 ii) Date of notification U/s 6 of the Act : 28.07.1997 iii) Date of award : 20.07.1999 iv) Area of the locality : Chandrawali @ Shahdara v) Project : MRTS, Delhi vi) The land use of area as per award : Residential vii) Petition referred to court on : 10.08.2010 (II) BACKGROUND:-
3.) The petitioner being owner of shop bearing no. No.1/1142- A, Main Market, Railway Road, Shahdara, Delhi situated in the revenue estate of Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara, Delhi- 110032, filed the present reference against the award No.1/1999- 2000 passed on 20.07.1999, thereby assessing the market value LAC No.7/18 Rajesh Vs. Union of India Pg No. 2 of 13 of the land @ Rs.2805/- per sq. yard which is not acceptable to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
The petitioner challenged the said Award on the following grounds:-
i) The petitioner was doing business in the said shop under the name and style of 'O.K. Silk Store' for commercial purposes.

The father of the petitioner has already expired on 08.12.1995 and other LRs of his father i.e. mother, four sisters and one brother had relinquished their share in the said shop in favour of the petitioner.
The shop was having top class construction and fully furnished with wooden work.

Other than petitioner, no other person has any right, title or interest in the shop and only At Present- 57/A vs ) Union Of India on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147840375/
2
petitioner is entitled to compensation/ enhanced compensation.

The petitioner is not satisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the LAC, determination of market value of land in question, measurement of land etc.
ii) The LAC has mistakenly assessed the market value of land and structures of petitioners at low rates which does not represents the market value of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA, Act.
iii) The market value assessed by the LAC was without making any on spot inquiry and without considering the principle of demand and supply.
iv) The LAC has valued the land in question @ Rs.2805/- per sq.mt. only whereas as on the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act, the market value was more than Rs.2,00,000/-.
The LAC has not taken into consideration the claims filed by petitioners before announcing the award.

v) The LAC has further failed to consider that the said LAC No.7/18 Rajesh Vs. Union of India Pg No. 3 of 13 property is situated at the heart of main market on Railway Road, Shahdara and the sale rates of commercial properties in the vicinity were also not appreciated.

entities.text: LAC No.7/18 Rajesh Vs. Union of India Pg No. 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the sale consideration of land in commercial complexes markters sold by DDA and other agencies has not been considered.

vi) In addition, LAC has failed to appreciate that land in question were situated in the main market,
Railway Road, Shahdara and surrounded by fully developed market from all sides.
All the amenities like electricity, mettled road, water, sewage, railway station, banks highway etc. were available prior to the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act.

Even Shahdara Railway Station is about 15-20 sq.yds.
away from the acquired land.
Banks, NH no.1, cinema halls, hospitals, Old Shahdara Court etc. were also situated near the acquired land.

The LAC has failed to appreciate the fact that Main Market,
Railway Road, Shahdara is one of the oldest market of Trans Yamuna Area.
vii) The LAC has not considered that properties in question were assessed to tax on commercial rates and had commercial electricity/ water connections.
viii) The petitioners had to shift their well settled business to some other place and there was no provision for providing compensation to petitioners in this regard.
No alternative sites have been provided to the petitioners before announcing the award, as per the scheme of Central Government.
ix) The market value of the acquired land at the time of notification U/s 4 was more than Rs.50,00,000/-, the petitioners claimed the same for their acquired properties and in addition,
petitioners claimed Rs.1,00,000/- and Rs.50,00,00/- as shifting charges and loss incurred by petitioners while shifting their place LAC No.7/18 Rajesh Vs. Union of India Pg No. 4 of 13 of business.

Petitioner is not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
LAC has taken into consideration all the factors including location and potentiality of the land while assessing the market value of the land.
The present reference petition is filed beyond the period of limitation and therefore, liable to be dismissed with cost.

c) The petitioner has also claimed interest, as per law.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.
d) According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land on 12.06.1997 and as such petitioner is entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e.
20.07.1999 till expiry of LAC No.7/18 Rajesh Vs. Union of India Pg No. 12 of 13 one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioner/ LRs of petitioner.
e) The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of compensation / solatium / additional benefits /
interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894, which have already been received by the petitioner, as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No. 01/1999- 2000 dated 20.07.1999.
f) The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties will bear their own costs.
A copy of this judgment be sent to LAC concerned to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioners within three months from today.
No order as to cost.
